question.text: Under Rule 3 of the PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005, reporting entities are required to maintain records of which of the following?

answer.text: Records of all cash transactions exceeding Rs. 10 lakh or its equivalent in any foreign currency
Records only of transactions reported as suspicious to FIU-IND
Records of all transactions regardless of amount or nature
Records only of cross-border wire transfers exceeding Rs. 5 lakh

explanation.text: The Logic: Rule 3 requires every reporting entity to maintain records of all cash transactions of the value of more than Rs. 10 lakh or its equivalent in foreign currency. This is a core category of record-keeping under the PML Rules. The Trap: Recording only suspicious transactions is insufficient — the Rules also mandate threshold-based records. Recording everything regardless of amount is not what the Rules require. Option D is false only because of the word "only" — cross-border wire transfers over Rs. 5 lakh are also a valid category, just not the exclusive one. Note: Reporting entities must also maintain records of series of integrally connected cash transactions in a month that individually fall below Rs. 10 lakh but aggregate above it.
